shadows.name: card

shadows.name: double-rule
shadows.purpose: Inner line of the double ink rule on menus, dice panel and card.

shadows.name: island-shadow
shadows.value: line layer #2c4a43, width 10→20px, blur 9→18px, translate [6, 7] map-anchored, opacity 0.72 fading out by zoom 8.5

motion.name: ease-print
motion.purpose: Card slide, menus, the cartouche unrolling.

motion.name: cartouche-unroll
motion.purpose: Signature moment when a place opens.

motion.name: rose-turn
motion.value: rotate(-bearing) on every map rotate event; tap eases bearing to 0 over 1s
motion.purpose: The compass rose turns live with the map.

motion.name: sea-names-fade
motion.purpose: Sea names leave when the view closes in.

motion.name: swell
motion.value: custom GPU layer: lines ~9px apart rolling shoreward at ~2.4px/s (scaled 2^((z-5)*0.45)), 15 fps clock
motion.purpose: The coast water-lines come alive as a swell (far view).

motion.name: creature-scenes
motion.value: whale 9s (rise, spout, tail, dive) every 30–55s; serpent 11s every 80–130s
motion.purpose: Rare sea creatures, as on antique charts.

motion.name: ship-voyage
motion.value: 3D bezaisen 22px tall at zoom 5, growing ×1.5 per zoom level (slower than the map): grow in 1.6s, 3px/s at zoom 5 straight to or from a port, roll ±0.07 rad / pitch ±0.035 rad, shrink away 1.6s, fade out between zoom 6.6 and 7.2; max 2, every 7–16s
motion.purpose: Edo ships crossing the open sea, far from the coasts.

motion.name: legend-idle
motion.value: per-vignette CSS loops of 0.5–5s (sway ±2.5°, fan ±11°, bob 1px, ground shake), only for vignettes inside the view; the bubble pans the map over 0.45s if it would sit under the top buttons; the bravo seal stamps in over 0.55s
motion.purpose: Hidden legends feel alive without crowding the map.

narrative.northStar: The old relief map on the table
narrative.overview:
The map is an antique relief map of Japan, the kind engraved and hand-tinted for a study wall. The islands are a shaded sepia model (pale sand on the coasts, ochre-tan hills, umber mountains and bone-white peaks) under a strong umber hillshade lit from the north-west. The sea is an aged, slightly faded turquoise: engraved water-lines hug every coast, and the islands cast a soft shadow onto it, so they stand up from the sheet. Seen from afar the sea lives a little: the water-lines roll in toward the shore, a small 3D Edo trading ship now and then crosses the open sea toward a port, and a whale blows or a sea serpent rises from time to time. A grain, faint foxing and burnt edges lie over the whole sheet. The seas are named in 17th-century italic copperplate, a compass rose turns with the map, and a rolled title scroll reads Japan · 日本 · Japon. The interface is made of parchment plates ruled in sepia ink, and cartographer's red marks what the visitor can do.

The owner chose this world on 2026-09-30 from three reference images: a parchment map with a scroll and a compass rose, a shaded beige relief on a turquoise sea, and an old geological relief map. It replaced the "Estampe" woodblock-print world (dark indigo). The map always leads; the interface stays small, square-cornered and flat.
keyCharacteristics: Aged turquoise sea with engraved water-lines and island shadows (far view only)
Sepia shaded relief; parchment sky and haze at the horizon
Aged-paper overlay (grain, foxing, vignette) between the relief and the places
Parchment plates with a double ink rule; 2px corners
Italic copperplate sea names lying on the water; vertical Japanese names in the Japanese UI
A compass rose that turns with the map, and a Japan · 日本 · Japon scroll bottom-left
Up close, every place is a small painted low-poly model of its category, standing on a base in the category colour
From afar, a living sea: swell rolling to the shore, a few 3D Edo ships far out at sea, a whale or a sea serpent now and then
Zoomed in, twenty-two hidden legend vignettes to find, each telling its story in a parchment bubble

rules.name: The Red Ink Is a Verb Rule
rules.body: Cartographer's red marks only what the visitor can do or has chosen. It has two ornamental uses, both ones a cartographer would make: the north point of the rose (which is itself a button), and the 日本 seal on the title scroll.

rules.name: The Sheet Owns the Hues Rule
rules.body: Category colours come from the owner's Google Sheet. The site ages each one toward sepia (`color-mix(in oklab, <colour> 78%, #4a3521)`) so any colour the owner picks sits in the engraving. Do not hard-code category colours.

rules.name: The Map Lettering Rule
rules.body: IM Fell English appears only on the map itself: sea names, prefecture names and the title scroll. Region names on the map, and names and titles in the interface, are Zen Antique. Buttons, labels, counts and reading text are always Noto Sans.

rules.name: The Far View Rule
rules.body: The coast ink, water-lines, island shadow and sea names belong to the whole-archipelago view. The line layers fade out between zoom 6.5 and 8.5, because the Natural Earth coastline is too coarse to match the relief close up. The sea names hide at zoom 6.2 and above, together with the switch from dots to crests.

rules.name: The Paper Under the Pins Rule
rules.body: The aged-paper overlay is inserted right after the map canvas: above the relief, but under the places and sea names, which stay crisp. It is one static image (a gradient plus two SVG turbulence textures) with normal alpha, and nothing in it recomputes while the map moves.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: No `backdrop-filter` and no `mix-blend-mode` over the map. Both are recomputed every frame while the map moves, and made phones stutter.

rules.name: The Living Sea Rule
rules.body: The sea moves only in the far view (below zoom 7.2), slowly and sparsely, on a 15 fps clock that stops when the page is hidden. The swell and the ships are custom GPU layers and the creatures are HTML markers with CSS motion, so nothing re-bakes the terrain textures. Ships stay far from the coasts and never number more than two: the owner removed the offshore wavelets and the coast-hugging routes because they crowded the map. Under reduced motion the sea is still: the three fixed water-lines return.

rules.name: The Open-Sea Mask Rule
rules.body: Everything farther than about 70 km from Japan, or nearer a neighbour than Japan, is painted the sea colour (masque-large.geojson), on top of the neighbours mask. Natural Earth misses thousands of tiny foreign islets, and from above they twinkled as sand specks whenever the map moved.

rules.name: The Hidden Legends Rule
rules.body: Legend vignettes appear only from zoom 6.5, where they are found like easter eggs, and sit under the place pins so places stay first. They share the creatures' ink-and-watercolour hand. The found counter appears only after the first find, and the list gives unknown legends' regions as hints, never their positions.

rules.name: The Inland Water Rule
rules.body: Lakes and the big rivers (OpenStreetMap) are painted in the sea colour over the relief, edged with the water-line ink. River width grows with zoom and river size; rivers under 100 km appear only from zoom 6.5. Like the coasts, they read as engraving: no gradients, no labels.

rules.name: The Hand-Coloured Border Rule
rules.body: Region borders are a dash-dot sepia line edged on each side by a soft watercolour band in that region's colour, as on hand-coloured atlases; prefecture borders are short sepia dashes that appear from zoom 6.5. Names follow the zoom: regions from 5.5 to 7.4, then prefectures. They lie under the paper, the legends and the pins.

dos: Do keep panels Parchment (#efe4c8) with a 1px Ink Rule (#8a6b45) border and 2px corners, and give the large ones (menus, dice panel, card) the double rule.
Do set interface names and titles in Zen Antique, map lettering in IM Fell English italic, and everything else in Noto Sans.
Do write in Sepia Ink (#35251a) on parchment, using its softer steps for secondary text, never grey.
Do keep the relief's sea stops transparent and paint the sea with the background, so the water-lines and island shadows show beneath.
Do use Cartographer's Red (#a8321f) only for actions and chosen states (plus the rose's north point and the 日本 seal).
donts: Don't use `backdrop-filter`, glass, blur or `mix-blend-mode` over the map.
Don't use pill shapes or corners above 3px on plates (circles are only for crests, dots, the rose and the logo).
Don't put colour-relief stops within about 1 m of 0 m: many phone GPUs read the sea as about −0.5 m.
Don't show unsoftened Sheet colours: always pass them through the sepia mix.
Don't draw a decorative border around the screen: the owner chose the scroll, rose, sea names and aged paper, and left the frame out.
Don't put a category label or kicker above a heading.

Don't animate map layers by changing their paint each frame: with terrain they are baked into tile textures, and every paint change re-bakes them all. Animate in a custom GPU layer or in HTML markers.
Don't show the legend vignettes in the far view: they are meant to be found by zooming in.
